title: Uno tras otro: describir una sucesión rápida de casos

sections.content: Uno tras otro (one after another) describes a rapid succession of similar cases -- useful for narrating a wave of comparable events across different countries or moments. It agrees in gender with what it refers to (uno tras otro / una tras otra). These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Entre 1979 y 1990, uno tras otro, la mayoría de los países regresaron a algún tipo de gobierno civil elegido.
items.english: Between 1979 and 1990, one after another, most of the countries returned to some kind of elected civilian government.

items.spanish: Uno tras otro, estos nuevos gobiernos civiles tuvieron que enfrentar la crisis de la deuda y las primeras reformas neoliberales.
items.english: One after another, these new civilian governments had to face the debt crisis and the first neoliberal reforms.

items.spanish: En las próximas lecciones examinaremos cómo estos países intentaron construir, uno tras otro, nuevas instituciones democráticas.
items.english: In the next lessons we'll examine how these countries tried to build, one after another, new democratic institutions.

items.spanish: Las dictaduras del Cono Sur cayeron, una tras otra, entre mediados de los años ochenta y comienzos de los noventa.
items.english: The Southern Cone dictatorships fell, one after another, between the mid-1980s and the early 1990s.

sections.content: Uno tras otro can slot into a sentence mid-clause, set off by commas, without disrupting the main structure -- it adds a sense of momentum to what would otherwise be a simple list.
